backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 81% of what happened (10% fell below it, 10% above) — about right. Loss-makers' operating margin three years out: inside its 80% range 71% of the time (448 outcomes). The chance of an operating profit within three years scores +0.02 against simply using the share that got there (Brier skill: above 0 is better than that base rate). Cash running out within three years: Brier skill -4.01 against the share that stopped filing (602 loss-makers; stopping includes acquisitions, so it overstates failures).

implied_return.note: The yearly return a buyer at today's price earns if each model's assumptions hold (an implied cost of capital). Above the cost of equity: the price leaves room; below: the price already asks for more than the models deliver.

methods.formula: Value = mean over paths of: 0 if the cash runs out, else (Σ FCFFₜ ÷ (1 + WACC)ᵗ + TV ÷ (1 + WACC)¹⁰ + cash − debt − claims) ÷ shares, floored at 0;  gₜ₊₁ = ḡ + φ(gₜ − ḡ) + σ_g ε;  mₜ₊₁ = mₜ + a − κ_loss mₜ + σ(mₜ) η while mₜ < 0, mₜ + κ(target − mₜ) + σ η once profitable;  FCFFₜ = NOPATₜ + D&A − capex − 10% × ΔRevenueₜ;  cashₜ = cashₜ₋₁(1 + r) + FCFFₜ + stock-based payₜ − interest (+ credit-line draws)
steps: start: revenue $153.5B, growth +4.9% (analysts), operating margin -17.1%, cash $0, debt $0

growth fades toward ḡ = 5.4% with persistence φ = 0.21, spread σ_g = 24.8 points; while losing money the margin changes by -0.7 points − 0.24 × the margin a year (surprise σ = 5.9 + 0.42 × |m| points), once profitable it is pulled toward 8.0% at κ = 0.05 (σ = 3.5 points); shock correlation ρ = 0.30
